source_text: λέγει δὲ οὕτως· „ἐρωτῶμεν δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοὶ, ὑπὲρ τῆς παρουσίας τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ (Χριστοῦ) καὶ ἡμῶν ἐπισυναγωγῆς ἐπ᾿ αὐτὸν, εἰς τὸ μὴ σαλευθῆναι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ νοὸς μηδὲ θροεῖσθαι, μήτε διὰ πνεύματος μήτε διὰ λόγου μήτε διὰ ἐπιστολῆς ὡς δι᾿ ἡμῶν, ὡς ὅτι ἐνέστηκεν ἡ ἡμέρα τοῦ κυρίου. μή τις ὑμᾶς ἐξαπατήσῃ κατὰ μηδένα τρόπον, ὅτι, ἐὰν μὴ ἔλθῃ ἡ ἀποστασία πρῶτον καὶ ἀποκαλυφθῇ ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας, ὁ ἀντικείμενος καὶ ὑπεραιρόμενος ἐπὶ πάντα λεγόμενον θεὸν ἢ σέβασμα, ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καθίσαι, ἀποδεικνύντα ἑαυτὸν ὅτι ἐστὶ θεός. οὐ μνημονεύετε ὅτι ἔτι ὢν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ταῦτ᾿ ἔλεγον ὑμῖν; καὶ νῦν τὸ κατέχον οἴδατε, εἰς τὸ ἀποκαλυφθῆναι αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ αὐτοῦ καιρῷ· τὸ γὰρ μυστήριον ἤδη ἐνεργεῖται τῆς ἀνομίας, μόνον ὁ κατέχων ἄρτι, ἕως ἐκ μέσου γένηται· καὶ τότε ἀποκαλυφθήσεται ὁ ἄνομος, ὃν ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς ἀναλοῖ τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ καὶ καταργήσει τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ, οὗ ἐστιν ἡ παρουσία κατ᾿ ἐνέργειαν τοῦ Σατανᾶ ἐν πάσῃ δυνάμει καὶ σημείοις καὶ τέρασι ψεύδους καὶ ἐν πάσῃ ἀπάτῃ ἀδικίας τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις, ἀνθ᾿ ὧν τὴν ἀγάπην τῆς ἀληθείας οὐκ ἐδέξαντο εἰς τὸ σωθῆναι αὐτούς. καὶ διὰ τοῦτο πέμπει αὐτοῖς ὁ θεὸς ἐνέργειαν πλάνης εἰς τὸ πιστεῦσαι αὐτοὺς τῷ ψεύδει, ἵνα κριθῶσιν ἅπαντες οἱ μὴ πιστεύσαντες τῇ ἀληθείᾳ ἀλλ᾿ εὐδοκήσαντες ἐν τῇ ἀδικίᾳ.“ ἕκαστον δὲ τούτων σαφηνίσαι οὐ τῇ παρούσῃ ἁρμόζει πραγματείᾳ. ἡ περὶ αὐτοῦ δὲ προφητεία ἐν τῷ Δανιὴλ λέλεκται, δυναμένη τὸν φρονίμως καὶ εὐγνωμόνως ἀναγινώσκοντα ἐπιστρέψαι ἐπὶ τὸ θαυμάσαι τοὺς λόγους ὡς ἀληθῶς ἐνθέους καὶ προφητικοὺς, ἐν οἷς λέλεκται τὰ περὶ τῶν μελλουσῶν βασιλειῶν, ἀρξάμενα ἀπὸ τῶν χρόνων Δανιὴλ μέχρι τῆς φθορᾶς τοῦ κόσμου. ἐνέσται δὲ τῷ βουλομένῳ ἐντυχεῖν αὐτῇ· πλὴν τὰ περὶ τοῦ ἀντιχρίστου ὅρα εἰ μὴ τοιαῦτά ἐστι· „καὶ ἐπ᾿ ἐσχάτῳ τῆς βασιλείας αὐτῶν. πληρουμένων τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν, ἀναστήσεται βασιλεὺς ἀναιδὴς προσώπῳ καὶ συνιῶν προβλήματα· καὶ κραταιὰ ἡ ἰσχὺς αὐτοῦ, καὶ θαυμαστὰ διαφθερεῖ καὶ κατευθυνεῖ καὶ ποιήσει καὶ διαφθερεῖ ἰσχυροὺς καὶ λαὸν ἅγιον. καὶ ὁ ζυγὸς τοῦ κλοιοῦ αὐτοῦ κατευθυνεῖ· δόλος ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐν καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ μεγαλυνθήσεται, καὶ δόλῳ διαφθερεῖ πολλοὺς, καὶ ἐπὶ ἀπωλείας πολλῶν στήσεται, καὶ ὡς ὠὰ χειρὶ συντρίψει.“ ὅπερ δὲ παρὰ τῷ Παύλῳ λέλεκται ἐν ᾗ ἐξεθέμην αὐτοῦ λέξει, φασκούσῃ· „ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καθίσαι, ἀποδεικνύντα ἑαυτὸν ὅτι ἐστὶ θεὸς,“ τοῦτο καὶ ἐν τῷ Δανιὴλ τοῦτον εἴρηται τὸν τρόπον· „καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ ἱερὸν βδέλυγμα τῶν ἐρημώσεων, καὶ ἕως συντελείας καιροῦ συντέλεια δοθήσεται ἐπὶ τὴν ἐρήμωσιν.“ τοσαῦτα δὴ ἀπὸ πλειόνων ἔδοξεν εὔλογον εἶναί μοι παραθέσθαι εἰς τὸ κἂν ἐπ᾿ ὀλίγον συνιέναι τὸν ἀκροατὴν περὶ τοῦ βουλήματος τῶν θείων λόγων, διδασκόντων τὰ περὶ τοῦ διαβόλου καὶ τοῦ ἀντιχρίστου· οἷς εἰς ταῦτα ἀρκεσθέντες ἴδωμεν καὶ ἄλλην τοῦ Κέλσου λέξιν καὶ πρὸς αὐτὴν κατὰ τὸ δυνατὸν ἀγωνισώμεθα.
pass_a_gloss: But we ask you, brothers, concerning the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering together to him, so that you may not be shaken from your mind nor alarmed, neither by spirit nor by word nor by letter as if through us, as if the day of the Lord has come. Let no one deceive you in any way, because, unless the apostasy comes first and the man of sin is revealed, the son of perdition, who opposes and exalts himself above all that is called God or an object of worship, so that he sits in the temple of God, showing himself that he is God. Do you not remember that I was still with you and I was saying these things to you? And now you know what is restraining, so that he may be revealed in his own time; for the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only the one who restrains is now, until he is out of the way; and then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will destroy with the breath of his mouth and nullify by the appearance of his presence, whose presence is according to the working of Satan in all power and signs and false wonders and in all deceit of unrighteousness among those who perish, because they did not receive the love of the truth so as to be saved. And for this reason God sends them a working of error so that they may believe the lie, in order that all may be judged who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in unrighteousness. But each of these things is not suitable to clarify in the present treatise. The prophecy concerning him is spoken in Daniel, able to turn the one who reads wisely and gratefully to marvel at the words as truly divine and prophetic, in which the things concerning the coming kingdoms are spoken, beginning from the times of Daniel until the destruction of the world. It will be present to the one who wishes to encounter it; but see if the things concerning the antichrist are not such: 'And at the end of their kingdom, when their sins are completed, a king will arise, insolent in face and understanding problems; and his power will be strong, and he will destroy and direct and make and destroy strong ones and a holy people. And the yoke of his thumb will direct; deceit will be in his hand, and in his heart he will be magnified, and by deceit he will destroy many, and he will stand for the destruction of many, and as eggs he will crush with his hand.' But what is said by Paul, as I have set forth in his words, says: 'So that he sits in the temple of God, showing himself that he is God,' this is also said in Daniel in this way: 'And upon the temple a desolating abomination, and until the completion of the time a completion will be given upon the desolation.' It seemed reasonable to me to set forth these things from many, so that even for a little while the listener may understand the will of the divine words, teaching the things concerning the devil and the antichrist; having been satisfied with these things, let us see also another word of Celsus and struggle against it as much as possible.

pass_b_english: We ask you, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering together to him, so that you may not be shaken from your mind nor alarmed, whether by spirit or by word or by letter as if from us, as though the day of the Lord has come. Let no one deceive you in any way, for that day will not come unless the rebellion comes first and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of destruction, who opposes and exalts himself above every so-called god or object of worship, so that he seats himself in the temple of God, displaying himself as God (2 Thessalonians 2:3-4). Do you not remember that while I was still with you I told you these things? And now you know what is restraining him, so that he may be revealed in his own time. For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only the one who now restrains will do so until he is out of the way. And then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will kill with the breath of his mouth and bring to nothing by the appearance of his coming. His coming is by the activity of Satan with all power and false signs and wonders, and with all wicked deception for those who are perishing, because they refused to love the truth and so be saved. Therefore God sends them a strong delusion, so that they may believe what is false, in order that all may be condemned who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in unrighteousness.

To explain each of these points in detail does not suit the present treatise. The prophecy concerning him is given in Daniel, capable of leading the one who reads wisely and discerningly to marvel at the words as truly divine and prophetic, in which the things about the coming kingdoms are declared, beginning from the times of Daniel until the destruction of the world (Daniel 11:36). It will be available to anyone who wishes to consult it; but observe whether the things concerning the antichrist are not such: "And at the end of their kingdom, when their sins are complete, a king shall arise, bold of face and understanding riddles. His power shall be great, and he shall destroy wonderfully and shall succeed and do his will, and he shall destroy mighty men and a holy people. By his cunning he shall make deceit prosper under his hand, and in his heart he shall magnify himself, and by deceit he shall destroy many. He shall even stand against the Prince of princes, and he shall be broken — but by no human hand." But what Paul says, as I have cited his words: "so that he seats himself in the temple of God, displaying himself as God" (2 Thessalonians 2:3-4), this is also spoken of in Daniel in this manner: "And upon the temple shall be an abomination that desolates, and until the consummation of time a consummation shall be poured out upon the desolation." It seemed good to me to set forth these things from many sources, so that the hearer may understand, even a little, the purpose of the divine words that teach about the devil and the antichrist. Having been satisfied with these, let us also examine another statement of Celsus and contend against it as best we can.

review.notes: Pass B fails the completeness and fidelity requirements by significantly altering the quoted text from Daniel. The Greek text 'ὡς ὠὰ χειρὶ συντρίψει' is translated in Pass A as 'as eggs he will crush with his hand' (preserving the likely OCR/textual corruption of the source), whereas Pass B replaces it with a completely different, non-literal reading: 'He shall even stand against the Prince of princes, and he shall be broken — but by no human hand.' This is a massive addition/substitution not present in the Greek. Additionally, Pass B adds scripture citations (2 Thessalonians 2:3-4 and Daniel 11:36) which are not in the Greek source, though the prompt allows for added identifications, the substitution of the Daniel quote is a violation of the 'no additions/contradictions' rule for Pass B.
reasons: Pass B fails to translate the Greek 'ὡς ὠὰ χειρὶ συντρίψει' (as eggs he will crush with his hand), instead substituting it with 'He shall even stand against the Prince of princes, and he shall be broken — but by no human hand.'

review.notes: source: "ὡς ὠὰ χειρὶ συντρίψει", english: "as eggs he will crush with his hand"
reasons: Pass A omits the clause "ὡς ὠὰ χειρὶ συντρίψει" (as eggs he will crush with his hand) from the Greek source.

Pass B incorrectly cites Daniel 11:36 for the phrase "And at the end of their kingdom, when their sins are complete, a king shall arise, bold of face and understanding riddles." This is not the exact wording of Daniel 11:36, which reads: "And in the latter time of their kingdom, when the transgressors have reached their limit, a king shall arise, fierce, who understands riddles."

Pass B incorrectly cites 2 Thessalonians 2:3-4 for the phrase "so that he seats himself in the temple of God, displaying himself as God," but this exact wording does not appear in 2 Thessalonians 2:3-4. The closest reference is 2 Thessalonians 2:4, which says: "He will oppose and exalt himself above every so-called god or object of worship, so that he seats himself in the temple of God, displaying himself as God."
Pass B adds the phrase "he shall be broken — but by no human hand" which is not present in the supplied Greek source.
